children: OTTAWA--Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there's been a "slight intensification" in talks with the Trump administration on a revised crossborder-trade pact.

Carney, however, played down prospects for an imminent deal. President Trump this past weekend, at a rally in Michigan, said an agreement could be reached soon, without elaborating. National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett also signaled a pickup in talks.

"There is no change in the position of Canada," said Carney, speaking to reporters following meetings Monday with indigenous leaders. He said Canadian negotiators stand ready to agree to a pact that is fair to the country. Officials, among them Carney, have said the pact must incorporate tariff relief from Washington on goods like steel, aluminum and automobiles.
Carney said a deal is possible so long as the U.S. moves toward Canada's demands.

Talks on a crossborder trade pact collapsed back in August, with both sides accusing the other of making last-minute demands. In response, the U.S. and Canada have slapped additional duties on some of their neighbors' products, and Trump has vowed to double the existing tariff on Canadian-made motor vehicles to 50% starting Jan. 1.
